To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the formation of Ag(I)-mediates DNA duplex and triple strand by introducing a pair or triplet of pyridine base was successfully achieved, respectively, and the stability of these structures was significantly enhanced by Ag(I).
the Ag(I)-mediates alternative DNA base pair or base triplet through the incorporation of a pair of pyrimidine nucleobases in a DNA sequence.

we have accomplished Ag(I)-mediates DNA duplex and triple through a pair of pyrimidine nucleobases, and the Ag(I)-mediating base pair or triplet in a DNA duplex or tripe significantly stabilize the duplex or triplex.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and synthesis of artificial nucleobases for alternative base pairing through metal coordination, and with the development of metal ion-mediated DNA base pairing for the control of thermodynamic stability and the application of metal ions to the regulation of DNA structure.
the design and synthesis of novel nucleic acid analogues for metal-mediated base pairings, and the development of new DNA recognition systems.
the design, synthesis, characterization, and applications of artificial nucleobases for metal-mediated DNA base pairing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present Ag(I) complexation is the first successful example of the alternative base pair in DNA duplex, as well as the first example of the alternative nucleoside for DNA triplex.
we have accomplished the formation of Ag(I)-mediates DNA duplex and triple through the base pair of pyrimidine nucleobases.
the formation of Ag(I)-mediates base pairs or base triplets is a promising approach to the development of artificial nucleosides for alternative DNA base pairings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a metal complexation can be used as a new strategy for DNA base pairing.
the metal-mediated DNA base pairing can be a new tool for regulating the thermodynamic stability of duplex and triplex DNA.
the pyridine nucleosides are a new class of nucleosides for alternative DNA base pair formation through metal complexation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of a stable DNA duplex and triple-stranded DNA can be controlled through the metal complexation.
the Ag(I) complex can act as an alternative base pair in DNA duplexes and triplexes.
we have demonstrated the possibility of alternative base pairing through metal-mediated interactions.
